arxiv-1611-02431.title: Distributed recovery of jointly sparse signals under communication constraints Thanks: This work is supported by the European Commission in the framework of the FP7 Network of Excellence in Wireless COMmunications, Grant agreement n.318306, by the European Research Council under FP7 / ERC, Grant agr
arxiv-1611-02431.creator: Sophie M. Fosson, Javier Matamoros, Carles Antón-Haro, Enrico Magli
arxiv-1611-02431.description: Abstract The problem of the distributed recovery of jointly sparse signals has attracted much attention recently. Let us assume that the nodes of a network observe different sparse signals with common support; starting from linear, compressed measurements, and exploiting network communication, each node aims at reconstructing the support and the non-zero values of its observed signal.

arxiv-2005-14506.title: Deep convolutional tensor network
arxiv-2005-14506.creator: Philip Blagoveschensky, Anh-Huy Phan
arxiv-2005-14506.description: Abstract Neural networks have achieved state of the art results in many areas, supposedly due to parameter sharing, locality, and depth. Tensor networks (TNs) are linear algebraic representations of quantum many-body states based on their entanglement structure. TNs have found use in machine learning.

arxiv-2008-11243.title: Extending fibre nonlinear interference power modelling to account for general dual-polarisation 4D modulation formats Thanks: The authors are with the Information and Communication Theory Lab, Signal Processing Systems Group, Department of Electrical Engineering, Eindhoven University of Technology,
arxiv-2008-11243.creator: Gabriele Liga, Member, IEEE, Astrid Barreiro, Member, OSA, Hami Rabbani, Alex Alvarado
arxiv-2008-11243.description: Abstract In optical communications, four-dimensional (4D) modulation formats encode information onto the quadrature components of two arbitrary orthogonal states of polarisation of the optical field. These formats have recently regained attention due their potential power efficiency, nonlinearity tolerance, and ultimately to their still unexplored shaping gains.

arxiv-2203-14735.title: Partially accreted crusts of neutron stars
arxiv-2203-14735.creator: L.Suleiman, J.L. Zdunik, P. Haensel, M. Fortin
arxiv-2203-14735.description: Abstract Context. Neutron stars in low-mass binary systems are subject to accretion when material originating from the companion star accumulates on the surface. In most cases, the justified and common assumption in studying the properties of the neutron star crust is the fully accreted crust approximation.

arxiv-2206-06218.title: A proof of Frankl-Kupavskii’s conjecture on edge-union condition Thanks: Supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China under grant No.12271425
arxiv-2206-06218.creator: Hongliang Lu and Xuechun Zhang
arxiv-2206-06218.description: Abstract Abstract A 3-graph \mathcal{F} is U(s,2s+1) if for any s edges e_{1},...,e_{s}\in E(\mathcal{F}) , |e_{1}\cup...\cup e_{s}|\leq 2s+1 . Frankl and Kupavskii (2020) proposed the following conjecture: For any 3 -graph \mathcal{F} with n vertices, if \mathcal{F} is U(s,2s+1) , then e(\mathcal{F})\leq\max\left\{{n-1\choose 2},(n-s-1){s+1\choose 2}+{s+1\choose 3},{2s+1\choose 3}\right\}. In this paper, we confirm Frankl and Kupavskii’s conjecture.

arxiv-2305-12150.title: Super-exponential behaviors of out-of-time ordered correlators and Loschmidt echo in a non-Hermitian interacting system
arxiv-2305-12150.creator: Wen-Lei Zhao, Chao Han, Han Ke, Jie Liu
arxiv-2305-12150.description: Abstract We investigate the out-of-time ordered correlators and Loschmidt echo in a non-Hermitian interacting system governed by a Gross-Pitaevskii map model, which incorporates a periodically modulated complex strength of the nonlinear interaction as delta kicks. We uncover that the time evolutions of the out-of-time ordered correlators follow that of the Loschmidt echo in certain situations.

arxiv-2306-10623.title: Enhanced Masked Image Modeling for Analysis of Dental Panoramic Radiographs
arxiv-2306-10623.creator: Amani Almalki, Longin Jan Latecki
arxiv-2306-10623.description: Abstract The computer-assisted radiologic informative report has received increasing research attention to facilitate diagnosis and treatment planning for dental care providers. However, manual interpretation of dental images is limited, expensive, and time-consuming. Another barrier in dental imaging is the limited number of available images for training, which is a challenge in the era of deep learning.

arxiv-2311-18788.title: Automated interpretation of congenital heart disease from multi-view echocardiograms Journal: Medical Image Analysis
arxiv-2311-18788.creator: Jing Wang, Xiaofeng Liu, Fangyun Wang, Lin Zheng, Fengqiao Gao, Hanwen Zhang, Xin Zhang, Wanqing Xie, Binbin Wang
arxiv-2311-18788.description: Abstract Congenital heart disease (CHD) is the most common birth defect and the leading cause of neonate death in China. Clinical diagnosis can be based on the selected 2D key-frames from five views. Limited by the availability of multi-view data, most methods have to rely on the insufficient single view analysis.

arxiv-2312-12334.title: 𝒫 \mathcal{P} owMix: A Versatile Regularizer for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
arxiv-2312-12334.creator: Efthymios Georgiou, Yannis Avrithis, and Alexandros Potamianos
arxiv-2312-12334.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Efthymios Georgiou, Yannis Avrithis, and Alexandros Potamianos. Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) leverages heterogeneous data sources to interpret the complex nature of human sentiments. Despite significant progress in multimodal architecture design, the field lacks comprehensive regularization methods. This paper introduces 𝒫 \mathcal{P} owMix, a versatile embedding space regularizer that builds upon the strengths of unimodal mixing-based regularization approaches and introduces novel algorithmic components that are specifically tailored to multimodal tasks.

arxiv-2512-13021.title: Safe Control of Multi-Agent Systems with Minimal Communication
arxiv-2512-13021.creator: Mo Yang, Jing Yu, Necmiye Ozay
arxiv-2512-13021.description: Abstract In many multi-agent systems, communication is limited by bandwidth, latency, and energy constraints. Designing controllers that achieve coordination and safety with minimal communication is critical for scalable and reliable deployment. This paper presents a method for designing controllers that minimize inter-agent communication in multi-agent systems while satisfying safety and coordination requirements, while conforming to communication delay constraints.

arxiv-2512-16347.title: GWTC-4.0: Searches for Gravitational-Wave Lensing Signatures
arxiv-2512-16347.creator: The LIGO Scientific Collaboration, The Virgo Collaboration, The KAGRA Collaboration
arxiv-2512-16347.description: Abstract Gravitational waves can be gravitationally lensed by massive objects along their path. Depending on the lens mass and the lens–source geometry, this can lead to the observation of a single distorted signal or multiple repeated events with the same frequency evolution.
